what: A focused re-check of round 5's fixes (commit 616ced0): five checkers, one per group of fixes (ground caps, game of catch, far blast reach, two-player additions, page copy and tests), each told to break the fixes or find regressions they caused, and a skeptic reproducing each finding.
script: workflow rex-gui-b-verify-r5 (kept in history at the end of the run)

checked: Powers-off identity: node test/powers.js --off-only on a copy passes (15,541 cases, both passes). node test/powers.js --skip-off: 111/111. node test/shots.js: exit 0. Every round 5 ground-cap branch sits behind an Unbreakable footing or own-recoil guard.

Stomp shaking against effort (scratch stomp-mono.js). Checked 9 surfaces (sand, gravel, softclay, stiffclay, asphalt, concrete, ice, steel, granite), Rex and Ollie, all four powers on and Unbreakable footing alone, from 10^1.5 to 10^34 kg plus Unlimited, in steps of 0.002 (all on) and 0.05. ppv at 5 m, ppv at 1.5 m and plaster reach never fall. Each realBreaks edge is continuous: sand 6,394.5 to 6,394.9 kg·m/s; gravel 8,982 to 8,986.5; concrete 7,185.9 to 7,188.6; granite 50,429 to 50,533. T is footPulse on both sides of every edge.

Stomp cap against hand calculation (stomp-hand.js). vEdge from inverting the Poncelet law equals a 200-step bisection of penetrationDepth at the kept print or 1 cm dent: sand 5.05508 m/s, gravel 19.1838, concrete 9.38241, granite 245.293. The cap equals J just below the flip (sand 6,394.90, gravel 8,986.50). Clay and hard ground stay at q·A·T (soft clay 2,567, concrete 49,753, granite 3.38e7 kg·m/s).
Unbounded stomp (stomp-c.js). From 10^27 to 10^34 and at Unlimited, J equals the cap and whole equals J + supplied. Concrete: 49,753 kg·m/s and plaster reach 3.59 m at every dial.

Jump landing feet floor. landV1 = sqrt(2·d·bear/m) is exactly where landRatioReal reaches 1 (sand v1 = 2.354 m/s, concrete 27.76 m/s). The feet's blow never falls with effort (sand flat at 1.651 mm/s at 5 m from 10^3.8 to 10^12.2). A landing that real ground bears shakes the ground exactly as without the cap.

Collide hit from above (collide.js). On sand, gravel, soft clay, stiff clay and concrete, for jump and stomp sources at 10^5 and 10^8, J = min(whole, max(0, Nmax - (mA+mB)·g)·T) to 1e-9. Sand gives 0 with supplied equal to whole. Soft clay gives 1,348.5 kg·m/s, matching (79,985 - 58,977 N) x 64.2 ms.

weakGround friction cap. A car thrown at 45 degrees on sand at 1e6 kg with own recoil off gives J = 1,505 = 0.58 x 40,423 N x 64.2 ms, with suppliedDown 82,211 and suppliedSide 80,706. The page text gives the same figures (1,500; 82,000; 81,000). Bolted keeps the sideways part whole (a 30-degree throw: J = whole x cos 30). Straight up at Unlimited the ground takes the cap, 96,770 kg·m/s. The friction cap creates no shaking drops of its own: the drops in friction-footing throws also occur where suppliedSide is 0, and they come from earlier push-model steps.

Momentum bookkeeping: J + supplied = whole for the stomp, Collide and every vertical push checked. The exceptions are the angled unbounded push (finding 1) and the stomp's displayed whole near c (finding 3).
Jump shaking against effort on 7 surfaces with powers on, Unbreakable alone and off (jump-mono.js, jump-land.js). Shaking falls with powers on; see finding 2.

findings.expected: Round 5 says it fixed copy-infinite-push-uncapped: 'the Throw text must not say the ground can bear a push it calls ∞× its limit', and an angled push 'keeps its infinite sideways part only when bolted'. By that rule the downward part is infinite and capped: the ground can't bear it, and their power supplies suppliedDown = Infinity. So supplied should be Infinity, suppliedSide 0, and the text should say the ground takes the sideways part whole and only what it can bear of the downward part. Engine results should never carry NaN.
findings.fix: In weakGround: const dn = Jd > Jdg ? Jd - Jdg : 0, sd = Jh > Jhg ? Jh - Jhg : 0; return { J: Math.hypot(Jhg, Jdg), whole: J, supplied: dn + sd, suppliedDown: dn, suppliedSide: sd, sideTaken: Jhg }. In suppliedText, replace the side test at line 1243 with (x.sideTaken > 0 && x.suppliedDown > 0), since the old whole - J - supplied test is NaN for an unbounded push. I tested this on a patched copy (labp). There is no NaN in any case above. The Unlimited 45-degree text becomes 'Of that push (unbounded), the ground takes the sideways part whole and only what it can bear of the downward part, unbounded in all; their power supplies the other unbounded of the downward part'. The finite text is unchanged (sand, 30 degrees, 1e6 kg). Add a powers.js check: Unlimited, 45 degrees, default powers, supplied === Infinity and no NaN field.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced in the engine and on the page, and round 5 caused it. Before 616ced0, weakGround started with `!isFinite(J) ... return { J }`. Round 5 removed that guard so that unbounded pushes get capped. It also made bolted footing set capH = Infinity. For an angled unbounded push with bolted footing, Jh = Infinity and Jhg = min(Infinity, Infinity) = Infinity, so `suppliedSide: Jh - Jhg` is Infinity - Infinity = NaN, and so is `supplied`.

Engine (car, concrete or sand, F = Infinity, four powers on, or Unbreakable footing with anchor 'bolted'):
- At 30, 45, 60 and 89 degrees: toGround = {J: Infinity, whole: Infinity, supplied: NaN, suppliedDown: Infinity, suppliedSide: NaN, T: 0.0642}.
- throwPartner at 45 and 75 degrees: the same NaN.
- At 90 degrees it is fine: J 96,770, supplied Infinity, suppliedSide 0.
- With anchor 'friction' and no own recoil it is fine.
- Powers off is unchanged: {J: Infinity}.

Page: {action: throw, obj: car, angle: 45, inf: true} at all-out is the default state with the dial on Unlimited. The Throw item reads: 'The throw drives his feet down with ∞× what the concrete slab can carry. ... His legs spread the push into the ground over 64 ms, and over that time the ground can bear it, so it takes the whole push (unbounded).' The page's test `r.toGround.supplied > 0` is false for NaN, so it takes the 'can bear it' branch.

At a 10^30 kg dial and the same 45 degrees, the page correctly says 'the ground takes the sideways part whole and only what it can bear of the downward part ... their power supplies the other 17 sextillion kg·m/s of the downward part'. So Unlimited contradicts both its own '∞× what it can carry' and the finite limit. That is the very contradiction round 5's copy-infinite-push-uncapped was meant to remove ('The Throw text must not say the ground can bear a push it calls ∞× its limit'). The fix holds only at 90 degrees. The Wrestle throw at Unlimited, 45 degrees, also quietly drops the supplied sentence, because suppliedText returns '' for NaN.

What's correct, by README's rule (Known limits: bolted, the planet takes the sideways part whole; downward, at most bearing beyond the weight × T):
- The ground's take is J = hypot(Infinity, cap) = Infinity.
- suppliedDown = Infinity and suppliedSide = 0, so supplied = Infinity, not NaN.

The test does not cover this. powers.js check 5c ('unbounded pushes with a push time are capped') tests only straight up.

The proposed fix works. I applied it to a scratch copy:
- In weakGround: `const dn = Jd > Jdg ? Jd - Jdg : 0, sd = Jh > Jhg ? Jh - Jhg : 0; return {..., supplied: dn + sd, suppliedDown: dn, suppliedSide: sd, sideTaken: Jhg}`.
- In suppliedText: replace the `Math.abs(x.whole - x.J - x.supplied) > 1e-6 * x.whole` test, which is NaN when unbounded, with `x.sideTaken > 0 && x.suppliedDown > 0`.

Results with the fix:
- No NaN in any case above.
- The Unlimited 45-degree text becomes 'the ground takes the sideways part whole and only what it can bear of the downward part, unbounded in all; their power supplies the other unbounded of the downward part'.
- The 10^30 45-degree text and sand at 30 degrees, 10^6 kg, are unchanged.

Also add a powers.js check at 45 degrees and Unlimited: supplied === Infinity and no NaN field.

The all-out "At this effort it also ..." line lists no plaster. The landing item says the ground takes "only what it can bear, 56 kg·m/s" of 890,000.

powers.js checks only landings with landRatioReal <= 1, so it can't catch this. The test's own title doesn't claim a monotonic jump.

Scope:
- The engine behaviour predates round 5. The e692a27 engine gives identical drops. The page's own comment ("a hazard can switch off again at higher effort") expects it.
- What round 5 changed and got wrong is the claim. Say instead that the jump's body stop and push-off hand the ground its bearing over a stop that gets shorter as effort rises, so their shaking can fall with effort, and the courtesy ceiling can name plaster damage that all-out doesn't cause.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this in the engine and on the page. Round 5's outcome for code-weak-cap-nonfinite says "the stomp's foot momentum comes from its energy where its speed rounds to c". The new line in MOVES.stomp.blow is `const Jw = isFinite(J) || !isFinite(r.E) ? J : Jat(r.vFoot, sqrt(E^2 + 2 E legEff c^2)/c)`, so it only uses the energy when vFoot rounds to exactly c, which is when momentumOf returns Infinity. When vFoot rounds to one step below c (c − 6e-8 m/s), vToMomentum clamps b to 1 − 1e-16. That gives a fixed gamma, and the momentum sticks at 2.609e18 kg·m/s whatever the energy is.

This happens inside the 10^27 to 10^34 range that round 5 said it had fixed: at 27.04, 27.13, 27.19, 27.27, 29.05, 29.66, 32.07 and 32.97. It also happens across the 10^26.4 to 10^27 band below it.

The shaking is unaffected, because J is still the cap (49,753 kg·m/s). Powers-off is unaffected, because the line sits inside the Unbreakable branch. What is wrong is the "whole" and "supplied" figures shown on the page. Round 5 also made the error stand out more: the neighbouring dials used to say "unbounded" and now give correct finite numbers, so the odd dial is out by up to 1.4 million times against them. The values at these dials are the same as before round 5 (I ran the e692a27 engine), so this is a fix that does not fully hold, not a new regression. It is in the exact line round 5 changed and is the same round-off defect that line was meant to remove, so it is in scope. Minor, because it changes only the stated figures, not the shaking or the hazards.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this with my own scripts, and it is a real defect that round 5 caused.

**What round 5 changed.** Commit 616ced0 changed sheathOnly from `keptFire.kept && fb.kind !== 'before' && isFinite(fb.E)` to `keptFire.kept && isFinite(fb.E)`. So with Things keep their form on, a throw now arrives as a sheath catch whatever share of its energy the air has heated. It used to become a 'fireball' once the air held half the energy.

**The flight time is not updated for that.** arriveFast still sets `out.time = Lc / fast.v`, and for a sheath `fast.v = fb.vLumpAt = v0 / (1 + x/γ)`. That is the speed the lump arrives at, which is its slowest speed. In the engine's own snowplow model, 1/v rises linearly with distance: 1/v(s) = (1 + x(s)/γ)/v0, with x proportional to s. So the real flight time is ∫ds/v = (Lc/v0)(1 + X/(2γ)), the average of 1/v at the two ends times Lc. The engine's figure is (Lc/v0)(1 + X/γ), so it is too long by (1 + X/γ)/(1 + X/(2γ)). Under the old kind test, X/γ stayed at or below 1, so the error was at most 1.33. With the test gone, it tends to 2.

**Engine check.** Script verify-catch/t1.js runs catchLeg on the baseball, fastball, with keepForm, unbreakable and ownRecoil on, and compares out.time with a Simpson integral of ds/v(s). I also checked the arrival speed independently, as v0/(1+X/γ) with X = k·ρ0·A·Lc/m, and it matches the engine's vArrive.

| 10^17 kg | 62 m | 50% | 583 ns | 451 ns | 1.29 (also in the old engine) |
| 10^17 kg | 200 m | 50% | 4.00 µs | 2.53 µs | 1.58 |
| 10^17 kg | 1 km | 0% | 155 µs | 80.4 µs | 1.93 |
| 10^15 kg | 1 km | 50% | 846 µs | 445 µs | 1.90 |
| 2e13 kg | 11.5 km | 0% | 1.51 s | 0.757 s | 1.995 |

**Page check.** Script verify-catch/pg.js renders the built dist/index.html with state `{logKg:15, duoAction:'catch', duoOpen:true, cObj:'baseball', cLogD:3, cStyle:'hard', airAbsorb:0.5, keepForm, unbreakable, ownRecoil}`, with duo-effort set to allout.

It is exact because 1/v is linear in distance, and it matched the integral to 4 digits (4.4518e-4 s against 4.452e-4 s). The round trip picks it up automatically. A powers.js check comparing L.time with this formula past the half-energy line would keep the error from coming back.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced. Both texts are new in 616ced0. README.md line 103 says "(half of it within fastAir's dHalf / share)". The engine comment on MOVES.throw.blastAt (engine.js line 3763) says "(fastAir's dHalf / k)".

The code already divides by k. In engine.js line 684, dHalf is `xHalf * unit / k`. Here k is the share of drag that still acts (dragFactor = 1 − airShare), and xHalf is the full-drag half-energy sweep. My script checked this with fastAirWithin. For the car at E = 7.32e15 J on a level throw, the energy left at exactly fastAir(...).dHalf is 0.500 for every k:
- k = 1: dHalf = 52.1 m
- k = 0.5: dHalf = 104.2 m
- k = 0.1 (90% absorbed): dHalf = 520.8 m

The page prints dHalf as it stands (app.html line 1413: 'half of it over the first ' + fmtDist(fa.dHalf)), so at 90% it reads "half of it over the first 521 m".

Taken literally, the README sends a reader to the wrong distance. Elsewhere in that paragraph "share" mostly means the absorbed share ("(1 − share) × what real air takes"). Read that way, the README gives 520.8 / 0.9 = 579 m, where 46.9% of the energy is still left. Read as k, as the engine comment writes it, it gives 520.8 / 0.1 = 5.2 km, where only 3.8% is left. Either way it divides by the share a second time, which contradicts the engine and the page's "521 m".

One charitable reading of the README holds up: "dHalf" taken as the full-drag length, with "share" meaning the share of drag that acts. But the text names the code field fastAir's dHalf, which already includes the 1/k. The engine comment applies the same division to that field. So as written, both state the wrong formula. Round 5's own finding evidence lists dHalf as 52 m / 104 m / 521 m / 5.21 km and then writes "dHalf/k", which looks like where the slip came from.

Impact: no computed number changes. fastAirWithin and the blast-reach solve both use the correct sweep k·d/unit. The defect is a false formula statement in the README (and a code comment), which a critic checking the README against the page would catch.

- README: "(half of it within fastAir's dHalf, the full-drag half length divided by the share of drag that still acts)".
- engine.js line 3763: "(fastAir's dHalf, which already includes the 1/k)".

His grip is mu N, so it reaches mu Nmax only when N passes Nmax, which means the cap there binds only when the ground fails downward. verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced. The sentence 'Where real ground would just have held, the cap starts at what real ground took (the stomp's print, the landing real ground just bears), so a harder push never shakes the ground less.' is new in round 5. It appears 0 times in the e692a27 README and once in 616ced0. The next sentence says the cap 'applies to a jump's push-off and landing, a throw ...', so a reader takes the guarantee to cover a jump. The engine does not behave that way. In jumpOnce the push-off take is still `Jg = T > 0 ? Math.min(p, bear * T) : 0` with T = push.t, and it has no floor. Round 5 floored only the stomp blow and the landing's feet blow (`cap(..., 2*legEff*landV1)`). The push time shrinks as he pushes harder, so the ground's share falls and the total shaking from a harder jump goes down.

Measured with Rex, comic mode, all four powers on, friction anchor, P.RESTRAINT.MOVES.jump.shake, ppvAt at 5 m (max over all sources).
- Concrete (real bearing 1.58e5 kgf), push-off share and length: 10^5.5 kgf 7.14e4 kg m/s; 10^8 3,986 over 2.62 ms; 10^9 1,261 over 0.83 ms; 10^10 399.
- Concrete, ppv at 5 m from all sources: 10^7.5 636 mm/s; 10^8 804; 10^8.5 767; 10^9 581; 10^10 593. So a 10x harder jump shakes the ground about 28% less from 10^8 to 10^9.
- Push-off felt reach (feelOnce 1.016 mm/s) on concrete: 225 m at 10^6, 74.5 m at 10^8, 31 m at 10^10. On sand: 15.2 m at 10^6, 5.06 m at 10^10.
- The landing's body blow, capped as min(J, landBear*L.t) with no floor, also falls slightly on sand: 9.9 mm/s at 10^8.5, 9.4 at 10^11.

The concrete figures match the checker's exactly (804/581 mm/s; 3,986/1,261 kg m/s; 2.6/0.83 ms). I didn't recheck the page's 22.5 m / 7.61 m sand texts; the page likely uses a different feel threshold. The reach falling with effort shows the same thing.

This is a false general claim in round 5's README text, not a style point. The engine's push-off model, bearing × push time, has been unchanged since before round 5 and is self-consistent. The powers.js 5c check is labelled 'a harder stomp never shakes the ground less, and a landing real ground bears shakes it as without the cap', and it does test just that. It only leaves the README's wider claim unchecked.

Minimal fix: narrow the README sentence to 'so a harder stomp, or the feet's blow of a harder landing, never shakes the ground less', and add that a jump's push-off (and the landing's body blow) takes bearing × push time, which shrinks as he pushes harder, so a harder jump can shake the ground less. Alternatively, floor the push-off at its value where F = real bearing, and the landing body blow at m·landV1. Then add the jump to the monotonic loop in powers.js 5c.
